source_title: Holiday Eating on a GLP-1 Program: Meant Highlights Coaching Support for Social Events, Travel, and Cravings
source_excerpt:
MANASSAS, Va. , Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Between family dinners, office parties, and travel days, the holiday season rarely leaves routines untouched, and for people on a GLP-1 program, it can raise a fresh set of practical questions. Meant is highlighting the coaching support built for those moments, aimed at everyday guidance rather than the clinical side of care.
Questions That Don't Wait for the Next Appointment
GLP-1 holiday eating comes with questions that don't fit neatly into an appointment, from what to do at a buffet to how to keep a routine on the road. Sleep, movement, and stress tend to shift in December as well, and they all touch how a person approaches food.
Meant does not diagnose or prescribe. Prescribing decisions are made case by case by licensed providers through OpenLoop Health , and treatment is not guaranteed for every applicant. Coaching sits alongside that clinical process, not in place of it.
Setting goals across nutrition, movement, sleep, and stress, including a plan for the weeks ahead.
Preparing for social situations such as gatherings, restaurant meals, and travel.
Talking through cravings and everyday habits, with practical strategies rather than rules.
Staying accountable through scheduled coach check-ins and a structured, guided program.
Coaching is optional. Care Coaches offer lifestyle guidance and are not dietitians, clinicians, or therapists, so medical questions go to the care team.
Readers who want to see how the online assessment and coaching fit together can visit Meant Health for an overview of the process.
Meant is a health and wellness technology company focused on personalized GLP-1 weight-care support delivered through telehealth. The platform combines an online clinical assessment, licensed oversight through OpenLoop Health, Care Coach support, and supplemental wellness resources.
